decisions.reason: The camera sits close to the firm's core optoelectronic and space heritage knowledge, so the firm can read early market feedback well and keep developing the product through its own R&D.
The modular navigation camera builds directly on established competence, and the successful HERA launch gives proven mission heritage that the firm can learn from and use commercially.

Space situational awareness extends the firm's sensor know-how into a growing market, and research cooperation plus EU projects give it the knowledge to refine the suite, though the fit is somewhat less close than for the core cameras.
The miniaturized LiDAR builds on the firm's docking sensor heritage and matches its move toward compact sensors, so the firm keeps it despite its lower visibility on the website.
The radiation-hard camera is closely tied to existing imaging competence and was only recently launched, which leaves enough time to interpret early results within long space program cycles.
The asteroid camera draws on the firm's deep-space mission experience, though its mission-specific character and minimal website presence add some risk of it being folded into other product lines.
